title: Hunts FH-016S: Player claim action, list/map and hints

source.ref: Split from FH-016 (2026-11-10): the read-only player page shipped; claiming and the map need the claim action and a map view.

detail:
Add the claim action on the player page (server action through applyClaim and hunt_claim_apply, gated by the claims switch), the list/map view of visited stops and the hint reveal. Done when: a player completes a Trail end to end from the page, a second device shows the same revision, and a hidden clue never reaches the page source. Requires: FH-016, FH-020. Owner role: Web.

The live player can reveal the current stop's hint by explicit request when claims are enabled and the signed-in player has an active run. Hint requests read the existing run without starting one. Future clues, place names and hints are omitted from the rendered page. The claim action still needs the signed placement flow and run-version mission binding. The map needs an authorized source of locations for visited stops, and the end-to-end Trail and second-device checks remain open.

Update (claim action branch): app/(main)/hunts/[slug]/play/actions.ts adds claimStopAction. A signed-in player enters the code printed at the stop; the action derives the profile, resolves the placement by code (live Hunt, same slug, not revoked), opens a run-bound claim token with openClaim and credits through claimAsPlayer (applyClaim, hunt_claim_apply), gated by the claims switch. The placement binding picks the mission, so no mission key comes from the request; the idempotency key is stable per player, run and placement. The page shows the form only for an active run with a playable stop, plus a visited-stops list of credited stops (components/hunts/visited-stops.tsx). Tests render the page markup and grep it for hidden clues, places and hints. Still open: the camera or scan entry on the page itself (the /hunts/p/[code] scan route covers scanning), run-version mission binding hardening and FH-049T before activation, an authorized source of locations for a map of visited stops (the list ships, no map), an end-to-end Trail completion test against a real database and the second-device same-revision check. Status stays open.
